name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: ['main']
  pull_request:
    branches: ['main']

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}

jobs:
  integrity:
    # prevents this action from running on forks
    if: github.repository_owner == 'vercel'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        node: [ 20 ]
    steps:
    - name: Checkout
      uses: actions/checkout@v3
    - name: Enable pnpm
      run: corepack enable pnpm
    - name: Use Node.js ${{ matrix.node }}
      uses: actions/setup-node@v3
      with:
        node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
        cache: 'pnpm'
    - name: Check pnpm
      run: pnpm --version
    - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
    - run: pnpm ci-check

  test:
    # prevents this action from running on forks
    if: github.repository_owner == 'vercel'
    name: Node.js ${{ matrix.node }} on ${{ matrix.os }}
    # Installing compiles the headless-gl dev dependency used by the canvas tests.
    timeout-minutes: 10
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest]
        # The headless-gl dev dependency requires Node.js 20+.
        node: [20, 22]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    permissions:
      contents: write # to be able to publish a GitHub release
      issues: write # to be able to comment on released issues
      pull-requests: write # to be able to comment on released pull requests
      id-token: write # required for npm trusted publishing (OIDC)
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Enable pnpm
        run: corepack enable pnpm
      - name: Use Node.js ${{ matrix.node }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
          cache: 'pnpm'
      - name: Check pnpm
        run: pnpm --version
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm build
      - run: pnpm test
      - name: Update npm for trusted publishing
        # actions/setup-node ships npm 10.x; OIDC trusted publishing needs >= 11.5.1
        if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest' && matrix.node == 22 && github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        run: npm install -g npm@latest
      - name: Maybe Release
        if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest' && matrix.node == 22 && github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: pnpm dlx semantic-release@25.0.5

name: PR
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, edited, synchronize]

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: amannn/action-semantic-pull-request@0b14f54ac155d88e12522156e52cb6e397745cfd
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

[package]
name = "satori-layout"
version = "0.0.0"
edition = "2021"
publish = false
description = "Taffy layout for Satori, compiled to WebAssembly."
license = "MPL-2.0"

[lib]
crate-type = ["cdylib"]

[dependencies]
# Taffy with the patches in `patches/taffy`, see `scripts/build-layout-wasm.mjs`.
taffy = { path = "target/taffy", default-features = false, features = ["std", "taffy_tree", "flexbox", "grid", "block_layout", "float_layout", "calc"] }
# Parses the stylesheets of `<style>` elements, see `src/css.rs`.
cssparser = { version = "0.38", default-features = false }
# Decodes WOFF2 fonts, see `decode_woff2`, with the patches in
# `patches/woff2-patched`.
woff2-patched = { path = "target/woff2-patched" }

[profile.release]
opt-level = "z"
lto = true
codegen-units = 1
panic = "abort"
strip = true

Here’s an overview of the basic usage: ```jsx // api.jsx import satori from 'satori' const svg = await satori(
hello, world
, { width: 600, height: 400, fonts: [ { name: 'Roboto', // Use `fs` (Node.js only) or `fetch` to read the font as Buffer/ArrayBuffer and provide `data` here. data: robotoArrayBuffer, weight: 400, style: 'normal', }, ], }, ) ``` Satori will render the element into a 600×400 SVG, and return the SVG string: ```js '' ``` To render it to a PNG, use [Sharp](https://sharp.pixelplumbing.com), which draws SVG with librsvg: ```js import sharp from 'sharp' const png = await sharp(Buffer.from(svg)).png().toBuffer() ``` Under the hood, it handles layout calculation, font, typography and more, to generate a SVG that matches the exact same HTML and CSS in a browser.
